Growing up we had a family friend that knew my mom since a child. I grew up calling her my grandma. I loved her so much. Her daughters I knew as my aunts. It didn’t click to me that we weren’t blood because it didn’t matter to me as a child, that woman was my grandma. Well when I was 12 I believe she passed from cancer, and it was time for her funeral. They had all of her grandkids sit in the front. So of course I made my way to the front to sit with the rest of the grandkids. This lady from her more distant family tapped my shoulder and asked what I was doing. I said I was sitting with my “cousins” and she looked at me and said only the grandkids were sitting there, and I said I was her grandkid, and she said no only her real grandkids. It broke my heart. All my life I knew her as my grandma and we were so close. Then it clicked to me that we aren’t blood related. She made me go sit in the back. I remember just looking around at all the people I called my family, at my “cousins” my “aunts” and I wondered if they didn’t see me the same way I saw them. From that time on I stopped going over to their houses, I stopped asking to call them or go to events with them. I stopped almost all contact. Now as an adult I’ve spoken the the woman I called my aunt and she said she had no idea why the woman said that to me, that she wishes I would’ve come to them sooner and told them what the woman said because they loved me so much and didn’t understand why I didn’t want to be around anymore. Maybe it sounds dramatic to yall but to me it broke my heart, not that I just couldn’t sit in front, just that being told I wasn’t family after spending my whole life with them knowing them only as my family, then being told I wasn’t really one of them.
